description:
What the weather and air traffic flow management were doing at one US airport over a past window:
the METARs it reported, and the ground delay programmes, ground stops, delay advisories and operations
plan lines the FAA Command Center issued for it, with the condition the Command Center gave for each.

Measured, July 2026: on flights that reached an airport 15+ minutes late with their scheduled arrival inside a
Command Center programme the Command Center put down to weather, carriers coded 39% of the delay minutes as air
traffic system (NAS) and 9% as weather; on late flights to the same airports clear of any programme, 12% and 5%.

Use it to explain a delay or a cancellation after the fact: whether a flight left or arrived into a
thunderstorm, low cloud or a ground stop, when a programme started and ended, and whether the Command
Center called it weather, volume, equipment or staffing. Pair it with disruption_precedents
(kind="aircraft_day") for the flight's own times and coded cause; check both the departure and the
arrival airport, because a programme at the destination holds flights at their origin.

`airport`: three-letter FAA code as BTS writes it (EWR, ORD) or its ICAO form (KEWR); resolve a name with
resolve_airport first. Give `date`, the airport's LOCAL date (YYYY-MM-DD; the window is that local day),
or both `from_utc` and `to_utc` (ISO times, e.g. 2026-08-20T18:00Z; at most 48 hours).


NOT LIVE AND NOT A FORECAST: an archive of past days (the window held is in `provenance`). Weather is the METARs the airport reported, from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS archive (Iowa State University); programmes are the FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center's own advisories (fly.faa.gov); neither publisher endorses this tool. US airports only for programmes. Times are UTC unless a field says local. Reading the answer: `status` is resolved, none_found, not_covered (outside the window held -- never evidence that nothing happened), unresolved (the note says why) or unavailable. Read `programmes` first: each is one ground delay programme or ground stop for the airport, with `outcome` (ran, ran then cancelled, proposed only), `period_utc`, the Command Center's `impacting_condition` (e.g. WEATHER / THUNDERSTORMS, VOLUME / VOLUME, EQUIPMENT / OUTAGE, OTHER / STAFFING) and its delay figures (`average_delay_min_highest` is the highest average it announced, not any one flight's delay). `operations_plan_lines` quote the Command Center's plan where it names the airport. `weather.summary` gives thunderstorm reports, the lowest ceiling and visibility and the strongest wind and gust, each with its time; `weather.metars` are the reports as published. A notes entry that says advisories are NOT held for a day means a programme on that day would be missing. An impacting condition is the Command Center's reason for a programme, not the cause a carrier reported for any flight it held: compare with the flight's own times and coded cause. Copy `not_to_be_read_as` rather than soften it.
